verdict: UnitedHealth Group's operating profit surged 55% to $8.0B even though revenue barely grew, because medical costs fell, the care ratio dropped to 86.7%, and both the insurer and Optum earned more.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $112.0B in revenue, vs $111.6B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $3.74 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $6.38

kpis.label: Medical care ratio
kpis.note: Share of premiums paid out as medical care — helped by $860M of favorable reserve development

kpis.label: Earnings from operations
kpis.note: Up 55% vs $5.2B a year ago — UnitedHealthcare $3.9B, Optum $4.0B

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: Health-insurance premiums from members, employers and government programs — the money people pay for coverage. UnitedHealthcare served 48.5 million people in the quarter.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Prescription drugs and other products sold, mainly through Optum Rx pharmacies.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Fees for delivering care and for health technology and data services, mainly from Optum Health clinics and Optum Insight.

segments.name: Investment and other income
segments.note: Income from the company's investment portfolio and other small sources.

opex.name: Operating costs
opex.note: The day-to-day cost of running the company — people, technology and offices. At 12.7% of revenue (the operating cost ratio), it reflects targeted investment in infrastructure, AI and care delivery.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of buildings, equipment, software and acquired businesses over their useful lives.

otherDetail: Other expense of $1,023M is $962M of interest expense plus a $61M loss on subsidiaries held for sale (mainly the remaining South American businesses). Investment income is not in this line — it is already counted in revenue.
footerNote: Net earnings of $5,670M include $186M belonging to noncontrolling interests; $5,484M is attributable to common shareholders.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Profit rebounded while sales stood still
takeaways.text: Earnings from operations jumped 55% to $8.0B and EPS rose to $6.04 from $3.74, even as revenue grew just 0.4% to $112.0B. The recovery came from spending less on medical care, not from growth — and the company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $19.50–$20.00.

takeaways.title: Medical costs came down hard
takeaways.text: The medical care ratio — the share of premiums paid out as medical care — was 86.7%, and medical costs fell about $3.2B to $75.4B. Pricing and benefit redesign helped, as did $860M of favorable reserve development: care cost less than the money set aside for it, mostly for 2026 dates of service.

takeaways.title: Optum again out-earned the insurer
takeaways.text: UnitedHealthcare served 48.5 million people and earned $3.9B on $86.0B of revenue (a 4.6% margin). Optum supported more than 120 million consumers and earned $4.0B on $65.7B of revenue, with margins expanding 1.6 points year over year.

oneTimers: Below operating earnings, UnitedHealth booked a $61M loss on subsidiaries held for sale, tied to the remaining South American businesses it is exiting; the six-month total on that line is $133M.
The medical care ratio includes $860M of net favorable prior-period development — care that cost less than the reserves set aside for it — which flatters the quarter's medical-cost improvement.
